title: 1903 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship
text:
{{Short description|none}} {{Use dmy dates|date=April 2022}} {{Infobox Hurling All-Ireland | year = 1903 | image = | dates = | teams = | connacht = Galway | munster = Cork | leinster = Kilkenny | ulster = Antrim | matches = | poty = | team = Cork | titles = 6th | captain = [[Steva Riordan]] | manager = | team2 = London | captain2 = Paddy King | manager2 = | totalgoals = | totalpoints = | topscorer = | previous = [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship 1902|1902]] | next = [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship 1904|1904]] }} The '''1903 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship''' was the 17th staging of the [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship]], the [[Gaelic Athletic Association]]'s premier [[inter-county]] [[hurling]] tournament. [[Cork GAA|Cork]] were the [[1902 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|defending champions]].{{cite news|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/arid-20369932.html|title=Driven Dungourney’s hi-tech edge to help against Fenor|publisher=Irish Examiner|date=5 December 2015|accessdate=30 July 2026|first=|last=}}{{cite news|url=https://dungourneygaa.com/about-us/|title=About us|publisher=Dungourney GAA website|date=|accessdate=30 July 2026|first=|last=}}{{cite news|url=https://www.echolive.ie/corknews/arid-41668541.html|title=Nostalgia: Cork hurling remains a constant in a changing world|publisher=Echo Live|date=13 July 2025|accessdate=30 July 2026|first=|last=}} The [[#All-Ireland final|All-Ireland final]] was played on 12 November 1905 at the [[Croke Park|Jones' Road Grounds]] in [[Dublin]], between Cork and [[London GAA|London]], in what was their third consecutive meeting in the All-Ireland final. Cork won the match by 3–16 to 1–01 to claim their sixth All-Ireland title overall and a second consecutive title.{{cite news|url=https://finbarrconnolly.com/1903-all-ireland-hurling-final/|title=1903 All-Ireland Hurling Final|publisher=Finbarr Connolly website|date=|accessdate=30 July 2026|first=|last=}}{{cite news|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/gaa/hurling/not-since-1903-1919-have-cork-gone-so-long-without-a-hurling-all-ireland-has-their-time-come-again/a/135905739.html|title=Not since 1903-1919 have Cork gone so long without a hurling All-Ireland, has their time come again?|publisher=Irish Independent|date=28 July 2018|accessdate=30 July 2026|first=|last=}} ==Results== ===[[Connacht Senior Hurling Championship]]=== {{football box | date = Final | team1 = [[Galway GAA|Galway]] | score = won – lost | team2 = [[Roscommon GAA|Roscommon]] | goals1 = | goals2 = | stadium = }} ---- ===[[Leinster Senior Hurling Championship]]=== {{football box | date = 12 February 1905

Final | team1 = [[Cork GAA|Cork]] | score = 3–16 – 1-01 | team2 = [[London GAA|London]] | goals1 = | goals2 = | stadium = [[Croke Park|Jones's Road]], [[Dublin]] }} ==Championship statistics== ===Miscellaneous=== * Cork win their 6th All-Ireland title to draw level with Tipperary at the top of the all-time roll of honour. ==Sources== * Corry, Eoghan, ''The GAA Book of Lists'' (Hodder Headline Ireland, 2005). * Donegan, Des, ''The Complete Handbook of Gaelic Games'' (DBA Publications Limited, 2005). ==References== {{reflist}} {{Hurling All-Irelands}} [[Category:All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championships|1903]] [[Category:1903 in hurling|All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship]] [[Category:1903 in Irish sport]]
